instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: His most productive season and the closest he came to sustaining it: seven goals from the left in a side that survived on the last day.
His first full season and an immediate jump: left-sided, quick and much the most comfortable passer in the Liverpool back four.
Two goals and six assists, and for half a season Arsenal’s best player: an outstanding carrier of the ball in tight spaces. Output is the poorest possible guide to him.
Three years on from the Arsenal peak, by way of a failed move to Barcelona: a peripheral loan player whose sharpness had gone.
Signed in January on the strength of an outstanding left foot and a genuine passing range; slow, and the fitness was already a question at 22.
Thirty-five and well past his peak, but still a genuine Premier League starter: the running and the organisation outlast the legs.
Among the quickest forwards in the division and physically a handful; eleven goals is as much as the finishing ever produced.
A treble winner at twenty-two, playing off the front rather than as the controller he later became; rated for the passing range he already had.
A World Cup winner in his first Madrid season, remade from the attacking midfielder of the Bayern rows into the deep controller — the passing range was already the best in the league.
Thirty-one, a bit-part signing at Southampton and two years past his City peak; the movement had gone.
Twenty-one, quick and powerful, and error-prone enough that Spurs sold him within a year; the athlete was already top-flight, the defender was not.
Started a Champions League final and marked Pirlo out of a semi-final; the appearance numbers badly understate a tactically exceptional footballer.
A Euro 96 winner and a Bayern and Milan left wing-back; six goals and six assists for a lower-half side, and comfortably the best player in it.
A treble-winning squad, but injury and Carragher restricted him to eleven starts; rated below his Middlesbrough season on form, not on standing.
Eighteen, eleven starts and a season ended by a hamstring tear in March; already unplayable one-v-one, not yet the finisher or the creator. Rated as the teenager.
Thirty-four league goals, the Pichichi and a Ballon d’Or at twenty-two; level with the Henry anchor and bettered only by his own later seasons.
Forty-three league goals and eighteen assists in a treble: the most complete season of his career and the highest club-season in the database, behind only Maradona 1986.

Rated for the ability, not the outcome: a genuinely exceptional dribbler and the one player in a relegated City side who would have started for most of the division. Held under 80 because the end product was slight.
Persistent foot and hamstring injuries from 1994 effectively ended him as a top-level full-back; five starts in two seasons and a clear drop from the England regular of 1993/94.
Injured for half of it and still, when on the pitch, the most dangerous attacking player in the title-winning side — seven goals and nine assists from 14 starts at 20.
By Bayern he was a finished world-class player rather than the fragile prodigy of the Chelsea years — twelve league goals from eighteen starts and a Champions League final.
Two years past the Ballon d’Or and still one of the two or three best wide players alive: ten goals and fourteen assists in a title-winning side.
